deities: Shantadurga (Goddess Durga, mediator between Shiva and Vishnu)
festivals: Fatorpa Zatra / Zatrotsav (5 days, Paush Shuddha Panchami to Dashami, January) - Hathi Ambari, Fulancho Rath, Vijayrath and Maharath processions

history.dynasty: Bahmani Sultanate period (persecution); Portuguese period; Maratha period (reconstruction)
history.period: Idol moved to Fatorpa c. 1500 CE (per oral tradition); current temple post-17th/18th century
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 231 (Shree Shantadurga Fatarpekarin Temple, Fatorpa, Quepem) - same village, same name. Identity caveat: Fatorpa hosts both the Shantadurga Fatarpekarin temple and the famous Shree Shantadurga Kunkallikarin Devasthan; sources conflict over whether the famous January zatra (Hathi Ambari, Fulancho Rath, Maharath) belongs to the Fatarpekarin or the Kunkallikarin temple - a Gomantak Times zatra report attributes it to Fatarpekarin while other accounts credit Kunkallikarin, so the file 231 distinction ('famous zatra belongs to Kunkallikarin') may be wrong. Per the temple's own tradition, Kshatriya migrants from Narve Diwadi fled Bahmani Sultanate persecution (c. 1365-1370), sheltered the idol at Morpirla, and brought it to Fatorpa; 'Fatorpekarin' means 'she who is of Fatorpa' (fator = stone). The gomantak Times describes twelve vangods (communities) as custodians of the devasthan. The devasthan is in Fatorpa, Quepem taluka, South Goa - CSV town 'Quepem' is the taluka (verify: nearby sources also place it ~10 km from Quepem).

name: Shantadurga Temple (Fatorpa)
town_description: Fatorpa is a village in Quepem taluka, South Goa, about 10 km from Quepem town and 19-20 km from Margao, known for its famous Shantadurga temples and the January zatra. Surrounded by lush greenery, it is a quiet Goan hinterland village whose temple complex - spread over several acres - is one of the grandest holy sites in Goa.

travel.road: ~10 km from Quepem town; on the Cuncolim-Fatorpa road; local buses and taxis from Quepem and Cuncolim

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; January for the 5-day Fatorpa Zatra - the temple's biggest annual event (extremely crowded)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Exact daily hours unverified (verify); one travel guide reports the Fatorpa Shantadurga temple opens ~6:00 AM and closes ~8:30 PM
